entities.summary: The Iris flower data set or Fisher's Iris data set is a multivariate data set used and made famous by the British statistician and biologist Ronald Fisher in his 1936 paper The use of multiple measurements in taxonomic problems as an example of linear discriminant analysis. It is sometimes called Anderson's Iris data set because Edgar Anderson collected the data to quantify the morphologic variation of Iris flowers of three related species. Two of the three species were collected in the Gaspé Peninsula "all from the same pasture, and picked on the same day and measured at the same time by the same person with the same apparatus".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Iris flower data set played a crucial role in the development of linear discriminant analysis, a statistical technique used to classify objects into different categories. Its impact on machine learning and pattern recognition has been significant, with applications in image classification, speech recognition, and natural language processing.
